correctness.rationale: Independent uniform parent choices give exact tail p=a^m(a-1)!/(n-1)!; conditioning makes last m parents iid uniform on a older labels, yielding E[L|H>=m]=m+a(1-1/a)^m/2 (a=1 handled). Strict Bernoulli inequality gives positive exact tail-sum covariance. Eulerian leaf recursion, a bounded 1-dependent CLT, independence of early labels and late parent choices, and o_P(sqrt(n)) martingale leaf increments prove the joint Rayleigh/independent Gaussian limit. Gaussian tail domination proves covariance/sqrt(n)->sqrt(pi/2)/4. Actual standard-library verifier exhaustively checked all trees 3<=n<=9 and 3 large-n numerical cases, 178 assertions; these finite checks do not prove the infinite limit.

value.rationale: Youngest nonleaf label is a natural growth-age extreme with distinct Rayleigh behavior from the global Gaussian leaf count. The exact finite conditional regression and strictly positive covariance quantify a second-order dependence despite joint independence at leading scale; the sharp sqrt(n) covariance constant gives a genuine multiscale structural theorem, not merely a textbook leaf expectation.
